newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy shares end year with late losses, Fiat firm.
newsitem.headline: Italy shares end year with late losses, Fiat firm.

text.p: 1605 GMT - Italian shares ended the last trading session of 1996 with slight losses, slipping from firmer levels in late business after keeping to a very narrow range in an extremely thin New Year's Eve session, traders said.
Prices came off just ahead of the close in reaction to New York's fall as stronger than expected U.S. economic data surprised the markets there and sent shares and bonds falling.
But Fiat rose strongly following a government decision to give incentives to boost the depressed Italian car market.
* All-share Mibtel index closed 0.2 percent down at 10,571
* Mib30 blue chip index ended 0.52 percent off at 15,697
Fiat ended 5.49 percent higher at 4,590 lire after a day's high at 4,595 with over 13 million shares changing hands. Other stocks within the Turin-based industrial empire also performed well.
"The tone of the market is positive even if today it was mostly benefiting from Fiat buying," one dealer said.
Fiat-controlled Snia Bpd and Sorin Biomedica both gained, by 0.58 percent to 1,570 lire and by 9.04 percent to 5,850 lire respectively.
In weaker telecoms, Stet holding slipped 0.3 percent to 6,900 lire after touching a year's high of 6,990 early on.
The spin-off of yellow pages publisher Seat from Stet came into effect on Tuesday and the company will be listed on the bourse from January 2, a Stet statement confirmed.
Olivetti ended 2.06 percent higher at 535 after yo-yoing in the morning. Energy group ENI shed 1.38 percent to 7,785 lire.
